title: Kelly's temperament, handling money and his gold cornet
summary: Kelly was likeable but spent deposits on drink, so Robinson collected his own; Kelly kept pawning his small gold cornet.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Chris Kelly, the blues trumpeter and his band

blocks.x: You say, Chris and, uh, Chris and you used to kid together, what, did you have a good sense of humor? What was he in?
He's sort of, not likely to lose his temper, sorry.

Well, he was kind of hard headed, but he could be easy to conquer down. Yeah. Cause I used to conquer him plenty of times. But one thing I didn't like about him, you used to fool with your money so much. Yeah. In them days you always sign a contract and they give you a deposit. Oh yeah, I've heard of that. Now if you wouldn't be there with Chris, Chris would take that deposit and meet a couple of them little nitbits and get in the speedies and drink it all up. Yeah. It's time for pity now. Some of the men, that's why his band's gonna get short. But I used to manage to get up soon in the morning and catch him. When he started going out, we'd go together. Yeah. That's what we're doing. So when he'd get his deposit, I'd be ready to get mine. He'd be ready to get my hands. Yeah. Well, he used to like me all right. Cause he used to follow or nothing. I should be with him every day. See, I wasn't waking in the day then. I quit waking over there.
By the way, do you know what kind of a horn he used? Is the cornet trumpet or a sharp cornet or what did it look like?
When Chris died, Chris had with them one of them little bit of gold cornet, just about that long.
Yeah. One of them little bit of cornet. So he never did use a big long carpet then?
Chris used to pawn it all the time. Yeah. When he died, that was his pawn. Yeah. Oh boy.
